content: This medication is indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation in adults, with a recommended dosage of 3 mg taken orally once daily. It is also approved for the management of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults, with the same dosage regimen of 3 mg orally once daily. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established in individuals under 18 years of age. It is contraindicated in children under 6 years of age, as nonclinical studies have shown that a single oral dose caused fatalities due to dehydration in juvenile animal models. Use in children aged 6 to less than 18 years is not recommended, as clinical studies have not included sufficient numbers of patients in this age group to determine safety and efficacy. Caution is advised when prescribing this medication to elderly patients (≥65 years), as there is insufficient data to determine whether they respond differently compared to younger adults. Dose selection in elderly patients should be approached cautiously. Adverse reactions associated with this medication include diarrhea (5%), sinusitis, upper respiratory tract infections, abdominal distension, flatulence, abdominal tenderness, elevated liver enzymes (ALT and AST), hypersensitivity reactions (such as skin itching, hives, and rash), and vomiting. Severe diarrhea is rare but may occur; if it does, dosing should be discontinued, and the patient should be rehydrated. This medication is contraindicated in children under 6 years of age due to the risk of fatal dehydration observed in nonclinical studies involving young juvenile mice. It should also be avoided in children aged 6 to less than 18 years, as safety and effectiveness have not been established in this population. Additionally, it is contraindicated in patients with known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction. Severe diarrhea is infrequent but may occur. If severe diarrhea develops, the medication should be discontinued, and the patient should be rehydrated. There is insufficient data to assess the risks of major birth defects or miscarriage associated with this drug in humans. However, systemic absorption of the drug and its active metabolite is negligible, and maternal use is not expected to result in fetal exposure. It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in human breast milk. Given the negligible systemic absorption, maternal use is not expected to expose the breastfeeding infant to the drug. When considering use during breastfeeding, the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant from the drug or the underlying maternal condition. This medication is classified as a guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) agonist. It and its active metabolite bind to GC-C receptors and act locally on the luminal surface of intestinal epithelial cells. Activation of GC-C increases cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP), which stimulates the secretion of chloride and bicarbonate into the intestinal lumen, primarily through activation of the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) ion channel. This results in increased intestinal fluid and accelerated transit. Systemic absorption of the drug is negligible, and it is expected to have minimal tissue distribution. The drug is proteolytically metabolized into small peptides within the gastrointestinal tract. No human studies have been conducted to evaluate its pharmacokinetics. For patients with difficulty swallowing, the tablets can be crushed and administered orally in applesauce or water, or via a feeding tube. The medication may be taken with or without food. Tablets should be swallowed whole for each dose. If necessary, crushed tablets can be administered as described above (refer to oral preparation instructions). The medication should be stored at room temperature, between 20-25°C (68-77°F), with permissible excursions to 15-30°C (59-86°F). It should be kept in a dry place and protected from moisture.
